# AF 第七章 原文（重制基线）

## Chapter 7

[P01] It was a very cold winter. First there was stormy（暴风雨） weather, then sleet（雨夹雪） and snow, and then a hard frost（霜） until February. The animals worked on the windmill（风车） as best they could. They knew people outside were watching. If the mill（磨坊） was not finished on time, envious（嫉妒的） people would be glad. Out of spite（恶意）, people said they did not believe Snowball destroyed the windmill. They said it fell down because the walls were too thin. The animals knew that was not true.

[P02] Still, they decided to build the walls three feet thick this time, not eighteen inches as before. So they needed many more stones. For a long time, snow covered the quarry（采石场）. Later they made some progress, but the work was very hard. The animals did not feel as hopeful（有希望） as before. They were always cold and often hungry. Only Boxer and Clover never lost hope. Squealer gave speeches about the honour of labour（劳作）, but Boxer's strength and his cry "I will work harder!" gave more hope. In January, food ran short.

[P03] The corn ration（配给） was cut a lot, and they said they would give more potatoes instead. But then they found most potatoes were frozen in the clamps（夹子）, because they were not covered well enough. The potatoes were soft and had bad colour, and only a few could be eaten. For days, the animals had nothing to eat but chaff（谷壳） and mangels（饲料甜菜）. They would starve（饿死）. It was very important to hide this from the outside world.

[P04] The humans were glad the windmill fell. They made up lies about Animal Farm. They said the animals were dying（垂死） of hunger and disease. They said the animals fought each other. Napoleon knew this was bad. He wanted Mr. Whymper to spread a different story. Before, the animals hardly talked to Whymper on his weekly visits. Now some animals, mostly sheep, were told to say in front of him that they had more food.

[P05] Napoleon also told the animals to fill the almost empty（空的） food bins with sand. They put the little grain（谷物） left on top. Then Whymper was led to see the bins. He believed there was plenty of food, so he told the outside world that Animal Farm had no food shortage. But by late January, they clearly needed more grain. Napoleon now seldom came out. He stayed in the farmhouse（农舍） all the time, with fierce dogs at every door.

[P06] When he came out, it was like a big ceremony. Six dogs stayed close. They growled（咆哮） if anyone came near. Many Sundays he did not come. He sent orders through Squealer. One Sunday Squealer said the hens must give up their eggs. Napoleon had made a deal through Whymper for four hundred eggs a week. The money would buy grain to keep the farm going until summer. The hens made a terrible outcry（抗议）.

[P07] They were warned this hard thing might be needed, but did not believe it. They were getting nests ready for spring. They said taking the eggs now was murder. For the first time since Jones left, something like a rising began. Three young Black Minorca pullets led the hens, but Napoleon's wishes were not followed. The hens tried to stop Napoleon. They flew to the rafters（椽子） and laid eggs there. The eggs fell and broke on the floor. Napoleon acted fast and cruel. He stopped the hens' food. He said any animal who gave even one grain of corn to a hen must die.

[P08] The dogs made sure the animals obeyed（服从）. The hens held out for five days, then they gave in and went back to their boxes. Nine hens had died. Their bodies were buried in the orchard（果园）, and it was said they died of coccidiosis（球虫病）. Whymper heard nothing about this, and the eggs were delivered（递送） on time. A grocer（杂货商）'s van（货车） came to the farm once a week to take them away.

[P09] People said he was hiding on a neighbouring farm, Foxwood（狐林） or Pinchfield（窄地）. Napoleon was now on better terms with the other farmers. There was a pile of timber（木材） in the yard, put there ten years before when a small wood of beech（山毛榉） trees was cleared. The wood was good and dry, and Whymper told Napoleon to sell it. Mr. Pilkington and Mr. Frederick both wanted to buy it. Napoleon could not decide between them. People noticed that when he was about to agree with Frederick, Snowball was said to be hiding at Foxwood. When he leaned toward Pilkington, Snowball was said to be at Pinchfield. Then, early in the spring, something alarming was found.

[P10] Snowball was secretly visiting the farm at night! The animals were too worried to sleep. Every night, it was said, he did bad things. He stole the corn, knocked over the milk-pails（桶）, broke the eggs, walked on the seedbeds（苗床）, and bit the bark off the fruit trees. When anything went wrong, animals blamed（责备） Snowball. If a window was broken or a drain（排水） was blocked, Snowball did it, they said. When the key of the store-shed was lost, the whole farm believed Snowball threw it down the well.

[P11] Curiously, even after they found the key under a bag of meal, they still believed this. The cows all said Snowball came into their stalls（畜栏） and milked them in their sleep. The rats were bad that winter, and they said the rats were with Snowball. Napoleon ordered a full check of Snowball's activities. With his dogs, he walked around the farm buildings. The other animals followed far behind.

[P12] Napoleon stopped every few steps. He put his nose to the ground to find Snowball's footsteps. He sniffed（嗅） in every corner: in the barn（谷仓）, in the cow-shed, in the hen-houses, in the vegetable garden. He cried in a terrible voice, "Snowball! He has been here! I can smell him clearly!" When he said "Snowball," all the dogs gave terrible growls（咆哮） and showed their teeth. The animals were very frightened. It seemed to them that Snowball was some kind of unseen（看不见） power, filling the air around them and threatening（威胁的） them with all kinds of dangers.

[P13] In the evening Squealer called them together. He looked worried and said he had serious news. "Comrades（同志们）!" cried Squealer, jumping about nervously, "a terrible thing has been found. Snowball has sold himself to Frederick of Pinchfield Farm. Frederick is now planning to attack us and take our farm! Snowball will guide him. But there is worse. We thought Snowball's uprising（起义） was just from his vanity（虚荣） and ambition. But we were wrong, comrades. Do you know the real reason?

[P14] Snowball worked with Jones from the very start! He was Jones's secret helper all along. We have papers he left behind, and we only just found them. At the Battle of the Cowshed（牛棚）, did we not see how he tried to make us lose? Luckily he failed. The animals were too shocked to speak. This was even worse than Snowball breaking the windmill. They all remembered how Snowball ran in front of them at the Battle, how he cheered them on, and how he did not stop even when Jones's gun hurt his back.

[P15] At first it was hard to see how this fit with him being on Jones's side. Even Boxer, who seldom asked questions, was puzzled（困惑）. He lay down, tucked（塞进） his fore（前部） hoofs（蹄） under him, shut his eyes, and tried hard to think. "I do not believe that," he said. "Snowball fought bravely at the Battle of the Cowshed. I saw him myself. Did we not give him 'Animal Hero, first Class,' right after?" "That was our mistake, comrade（同志）. We know now—it is all written down in the secret papers—that he really tried to lead us to our doom（厄运）." "But he was wounded," said Boxer.

[P16] "We all saw him running with blood." "That was the plan!" cried Squealer. "Jones's shot only grazed（放牧） him. I could show you his own writing. Snowball was to give the signal（信号） to run away and leave the field to the enemy. He almost did it -- he WOULD have, if not for our heroic（英勇） Leader, Comrade Napoleon. Do you not remember how, when Jones and his men got inside the yard, Snowball suddenly turned and ran, and many animals followed him?

[P17] And do you not remember that just then, when all seemed lost, Comrade Napoleon jumped forward and cried 'Death to Humanity（人类）!' and bit Jones's leg? Surely you remember THAT, comrades?" cried Squealer. Now when Squealer told the story so clearly, it seemed to the animals that they did remember it. At least, they remembered that at the key moment Snowball had turned to run away. But Boxer was still a little worried. "I do not believe that Snowball was a traitor at the beginning," Boxer said.he said at last.

[P18] "What he did later is different. But at the Battle of the Cowshed, I think he was a good comrade." "Our Leader, Comrade Napoleon,""Our Leader, Comrade Napoleon," said Squealer, "has said clearly that Snowball was Jones's agent from the very start, long before anyone thought of the uprising." "Ah, that is different!""Ah, that is different!" said Boxer. "If Comrade Napoleon says so, it must be right." "That is the true spirit, comrade!" cried Squealer, but the animals noticed he gave Boxer a very ugly look. He turned to go, then stopped and said: "I warn every animal on this farm to keep his eyes very wide open."

[P19] We have reason to think some of Snowball's secret agents are hiding among us right now! Four days later, Napoleon ordered all the animals to the yard. He wore his two medals. His nine huge dogs jumped around him and made low sounds. All the animals were very afraid and bent down silently. They knew something terrible was about to happen. Napoleon looked at them seriously, then made a high, thin sound.

[P20] The dogs ran forward. Immediately they caught four pigs by the ear and pulled them, crying with pain, to Napoleon's feet. The pigs' ears were bleeding. Then three dogs jumped on Boxer. Boxer put out his big hoof（蹄）, caught a dog, and held him on the ground. The dog cried for mercy（仁慈）, and the other two ran away. Boxer looked at Napoleon to know if he should kill the dog or let it go.

[P21] Napoleon changed face and told Boxer to let the dog go. Boxer lifted his hoof, and the dog ran away, hurt and crying. Soon the noise died down. The four pigs waited, shaking, with guilt（罪行） on their faces. Napoleon called on them to confess（坦白） their crimes. They were the four pigs who had protested（抗议） when Napoleon ended the Sunday Meetings. They confessed（坦白） that they had been in touch with Snowball after he was driven out, that they had helped him destroy the windmill, and that they had agreed to hand over Animal Farm to Mr.

[P22] They said Snowball had been Jones's secret helper for years. Then the dogs killed them. Napoleon asked if any other animal had something to confess. The three hens who had led the failed fight about the eggs came forward. They said Snowball came in a dream and told them to disobey（违抗） Napoleon. They were killed too. Then a goose said she had hidden six ears of corn and eaten them at night.

[P23] Then a sheep said she had made the drinking water dirty. She said Snowball told her to do it. Two other sheep said they had killed an old ram（公羊）, a faithful（忠诚） follower of Napoleon. They chased（追赶） him around a fire when he was sick. They were all killed at once. The stories of confessions（坦白） and killings（杀戮） went on, until many dead bodies lay before Napoleon's feet. The air smelled of blood. When it was over, all the other animals, except the pigs and dogs, went away together.

[P24] They were very upset. They did not know which was worse—the animals who helped Snowball, or the killing they just saw. Long ago there were also bad killings, but now it felt worse because it was among themselves. Since Jones left, no animal had killed another. They went to the small hill where the half-built windmill stood. They all lay down together—Clover, Muriel, Benjamin, the cows, the sheep, and many geese and hens—everyone, but not the cat, who had gone just before Napoleon told them to gather（收集）.

[P25] For a while nobody spoke. Only Boxer stood. He moved about, his tail hitting his sides. At last he said: "I do not understand it. It must be our own fault. The answer is to work harder. I shall get up a full hour earlier." Then he walked off to the quarry.

[P26] When he got there, he picked up two loads（负载） of stone and pulled them to the windmill before he slept. The animals sat close around Clover and said nothing. From the small hill, they could see most of Animal Farm—the fields, the wood, the pool, and the farm buildings with smoke rising from the chimneys（烟囱）. It was a clear spring evening, and the low sun made the grass and hedges（树篱） shine like gold.

[P27] The farm had never looked so good to the animals. They were surprised it was their own farm, every bit of it. Clover looked down the hill and her eyes filled with tears. If she could speak, she would say this was not what they wanted years ago when they worked to end the human race. These terrible, bloody（血腥） scenes were not what they hoped for when old Major first moved them to fight. If she had any picture of the future, it was a society of animals free from hunger and the whip, all equal, each working as much as he could, the strong helping the weak, just as she had helped the lost baby ducks with her leg on the night of Major's speech.

[P28] But now, no one dared speak his mind. Fierce dogs ran everywhere. Friends were torn to pieces after they admitted（承认） bad crimes. She did not think of fighting back. They were still better off than in the days of Jones. Most of all, they must stop the humans from coming back. She would stay faithful, work hard, obey（服从） orders, and accept Napoleon as leader.

[P29] But still, this was not what she and the other animals had hoped and worked for. It was not for this that they built the windmill and faced Jones's gun. She thought this, but she had no words to say it. At last, she began to sing 'Animals of England'. The other animals around her sang it too. They sang it three times—very sweetly, but slowly and sadly, in a way they had never sung before. They had just finished the third time when Squealer came, with two dogs, looking like he had something important to say.

[P30] He said that, by a special order of Comrade Napoleon, 'Animals of England' was stopped. No one could sing it now. The animals were surprised. "Why?" cried Muriel. "It is not needed now, comrade," said Squealer coldly. "It was the song of the uprising, but the uprising is finished. The killing of the traitors was the last act. The enemy has been beaten. We wished for a better society. That society is now here. So this song has no use." The animals were afraid, and some might have spoken against it, but then the sheep began their bleating of "Four legs good, two legs bad." It went on for several minutes and ended the talk. So 'Animals of England' was heard no more.

[P31] Instead, Minimus the poet wrote a new song. It began: "Animal Farm, Animal Farm, Never through me shalt（将） thou（你） come to harm!" They sang it every Sunday after they raised the flag, but they felt it was not as good as 'Animals of England'.
